history.summary: The Someshwar Nath temple at Areraj, East Champaran, is one of North Bihar's most revered Shiva shrines; the CSV's 'Modern Shiva Temple, Areraj' is a misnomer - this is an ancient, living temple, not a modern one. Local tradition holds the Shivlinga is Swayambhu (self-manifested) and links it to the Ramayana/Treta Yuga era; a popular local claim says King Som erected the temple 2000 years ago based on the Shiv Puran (UNVERIFIED - no scholarly source corroborates). Areraj's documented antiquity rests more securely on the nearby Lauriya Areraj Ashokan pillar (249 BCE). The temple draws lakhs of Kanwariyas carrying Ganga water from Sultanganj during Shravan, plus pilgrims from Nepal. Distances/hours conflict across sources - marked (verify).

name: Modern Shiva Temple, Areraj
town_description: Areraj is a holy town in East Champaran district, about 28-30 km southwest of Motihari, and the headquarters of the Areraj subdivision. Once a village, it is now a Nagar Panchayat and is revered as a centre of Shiva worship in North Bihar. Its other major draw is the Lauriya Areraj Ashokan pillar, a 36.5-foot monolithic Mauryan edifice (249 BCE) that attracts tourists year-round.

travel.railway: Nearest major station: Motihari Junction (BMKI), ~25-30 km
travel.road: Areraj lies ~30 km southwest of Motihari by pucca road, connected via NH-28 and NH-104; buses and shared jeeps run from Motihari, Muzaffarpur, Bettiah and Patna

visitor_information.best_time: July-August (Shravan month, extremely crowded) and Mahashivratri for festivals; October-February for a pleasant visit
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): 4:30 AM-12:30 PM and 3:30 PM-9:00 PM per one source; around 5:00 AM-9:00 PM per another. Entry free.
